editorial.headline: Teaching the Skills Behind Craft and Industry
editorial.standfirst: KBLI 85597 covers private education in practical craft and industry skills, from batik and weaving to cooking, sewing and woodworking.
editorial.body:
KBLI 85597 is the classification for privately delivered education in craft and industrial skills: the kind of teaching that turns practical knowledge into a learnable trade. Its scope reaches from weaving, embroidery, batik, sewing and fashion to woodcarving, furniture, woodworking, screen printing, cooking, home-industry skills and other courses in making and craftsmanship. This is education with its hands in the material world—structured instruction rather than the production or sale of the resulting goods.

The activity is available across every listed business scale: Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar. That breadth matters because the classification accommodates both intimate skills courses and larger private education operations without changing the essential character of the activity. What binds the examples together is the provision of education or courses in practical craft and industry capabilities, whether the subject is a traditional technique, a household-enterprise skill or a more formal vocational craft.

At the national level, the activity is TERBUKA to PMA and its foreign-ownership ceiling is 100%. Put another way, the record authorizes full foreign ownership at the national level. The stated basis is Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. There is no lower foreign-ownership cap in this record to obscure the position: for this activity, the national ceiling is complete foreign ownership.

Bali does not reverse that result. The provincial moratorium blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis, but this activity is not blocked by that moratorium. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK. The record adds an important operational distinction at the Besar scale: the OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. That is not a prohibition; it is the reason the activity sits outside the moratorium’s blocked category. For a foreign investor considering a Bali-based private craft or industrial education business, the honest reading is therefore clear: PMA registration is not blocked here, while a Besar-scale operation carries the stated higher OSS risk classification.
